tools.name: Git
tools.summary: Distributed version control for source code and configuration.
tools.note: Use SSH keys or a credential manager; never paste access tokens into shell history.
tools.trouble: If a repository cannot be reached, check DNS, network access and the remote URL. For permission errors, verify the SSH key or HTTPS credential configuration.

tools.name: Python 3
tools.summary: Python runtime for scripting, automation and command-line utilities.
tools.note: Prefer virtual environments for project dependencies. Avoid installing project packages globally with elevated privileges.
tools.trouble: If pip is missing, check the distribution's Python packaging guidance. If a command is not found after installation, reopen the shell and check command -v python or command -v python3.

tools.name: OpenSSH
tools.summary: Secure remote login, file transfer and SSH key utilities.
tools.note: Termux sshd commonly listens on port 8022. Check the actual listening port before connecting. Do not expose an SSH server publicly without hardening.
tools.trouble: For 'connection refused', verify the server is running and the port is correct. For host-key warnings, confirm the server identity before changing known_hosts.

tools.name: tmux
tools.summary: Persistent terminal sessions and pane/window management.
tools.note: Start a session with tmux. Detach with Ctrl+B then D; reconnect with tmux attach.
tools.trouble: If the terminal reports a missing terminfo entry, update the terminal package and check the TERM value. Do not copy a configuration file from an unknown source.

tools.name: GNU Wget
tools.summary: Retrieve files over supported network protocols from the command line.
tools.note: Verify downloaded files and checksums before running them. Never pipe an unreviewed download directly into a shell.
tools.trouble: For certificate errors, check device date/time and CA certificates. Do not disable TLS verification as a workaround.

tools.name: jq
tools.summary: Parse, filter and transform JSON data from scripts and pipelines.
tools.note: Treat input as untrusted data; jq transforms data and does not validate the business meaning of a document.
tools.trouble: Use jq empty file.json to check syntax. If a field is null, inspect the input shape before changing the filter.

tools.name: ripgrep
tools.summary: Fast recursive text search with sensible defaults and ignore-file support.
tools.note: Hidden files and ignored paths are skipped by default. Use explicit options only when you understand the scope of the search.
tools.trouble: If expected files are missing, check .gitignore and ripgrep's ignore rules. Confirm the current working directory before broad searches.

tools.name: fd
tools.summary: Convenient, fast file and directory discovery from the terminal.
tools.note: On Debian/Ubuntu the executable is usually named fdfind to avoid a name conflict. The package is fd-find.
tools.trouble: If fd is not found on Debian/Ubuntu, try fdfind. Check PATH and the package's installed file list before creating aliases.

tools.name: tree
tools.summary: Display directory structures in a readable tree format.
tools.note: Use a specific project directory rather than scanning the entire filesystem.
tools.trouble: If output is too large, limit depth with tree -L 2. Permission-denied messages usually mean the current user cannot read a directory.

tools.name: htop
tools.summary: Interactive process and resource monitor for terminal sessions.
tools.note: Android may restrict visibility into other applications and processes. This is an operating-system permission boundary, not necessarily an installation fault.
tools.trouble: If process details are incomplete, check user permissions and platform restrictions. On a headless terminal, use top as a basic alternative.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.summary: Network discovery and service inventory for systems you own or are authorized to assess.
tools.note: On Termux without root, raw-packet features may be unavailable; TCP connect checks are the practical unprivileged path. Scan only authorized targets.
tools.trouble: If a scan reports a permission error, identify which scan mode requires raw sockets. Do not attempt to bypass Android or network controls.

tools.name: DNS Utilities (dig / nslookup)
tools.summary: Query DNS records and troubleshoot name resolution using dig and nslookup.
tools.note: DNS queries disclose the queried domain to the configured resolver. Use a resolver you trust.
tools.trouble: If dig is missing, confirm dnsutils installed successfully. Compare the default resolver with an explicitly selected trusted resolver to isolate local DNS issues.

tools.name: iproute2
tools.summary: Inspect interfaces, routes, neighbors and network link state with ip.
tools.note: Android kernels and permissions restrict some network changes. Read-only inspection may work even when configuration commands are denied.
tools.trouble: If an operation is not permitted, check Android kernel capabilities and privileges. Do not assume that installing the package grants permission to change interfaces or routes.

tools.name: Traceroute
tools.summary: Observe the network path toward a destination and help isolate routing delays.
tools.note: Intermediate routers may suppress or rate-limit probe responses. Missing hops do not prove that traffic is blocked.
tools.trouble: Try a different probe method only when supported by the local version. Check local firewall policy and compare with another trusted destination.

tools.name: iperf3
tools.summary: Measure throughput between two endpoints that you control.
tools.note: iperf3 server mode listens for incoming connections, commonly on TCP port 5201. Run it only on a trusted network and stop it when finished.
tools.trouble: If the client cannot connect, confirm the server is running, the port is reachable and both endpoints use compatible versions. Check firewall rules on both sides.

tools.name: OpenSSL
tools.summary: Inspect TLS certificates and perform common cryptographic and certificate operations.
tools.note: Protect private keys and avoid sharing them in logs or support requests. Use copies when experimenting with certificate files.
tools.trouble: For certificate verification failures, inspect the certificate chain, hostname, validity period and local CA store. Do not disable verification to hide an error.

tools.name: ShellCheck
tools.summary: Static analysis for Bash and POSIX shell scripts to catch common mistakes.
tools.note: ShellCheck reports likely defects; review each finding in the context of the script's intended behavior.
tools.trouble: If a warning seems incorrect, check the script's declared shell and interpreter. Do not silence whole categories without understanding the finding.

tools.name: shfmt
tools.summary: Format shell scripts consistently and make style reviews easier.
tools.note: Formatting can change many lines. Review the diff before committing or distributing a script.
tools.trouble: If the output style differs from the project, check the selected shell dialect and formatter options before reformatting the repository.

tools.name: fzf
tools.summary: Interactive fuzzy finder for files, command history and structured lists.
tools.note: Shell key bindings and completion are optional setup steps; inspect the installer output before adding shell startup configuration.
tools.trouble: If key bindings are unavailable, check the shell integration instructions and the active shell rc file. The fzf binary can still run without shell integration.

tools.name: socat
tools.summary: Connect or relay data between supported address types and sockets.
tools.note: socat can create listeners and forward traffic. Use it only with endpoints and ports you control.
tools.trouble: For bind failures, check address syntax, port conflicts and local permissions. Review both endpoints carefully before starting a relay.

tools.name: WHOIS
tools.summary: Look up publicly available domain and IP registration information.
tools.note: WHOIS output varies by registry and may be redacted or rate-limited. It is not proof of ownership or current service availability.
tools.trouble: If a server does not respond, try again later or use the registry's official lookup service. Do not treat missing data as a negative result.

tools.name: lsof
tools.summary: List open files, sockets and process-to-file relationships.
tools.note: Android restricts visibility into other applications. Expect results to be limited to processes your app is allowed to inspect.
tools.trouble: If a process is missing, check user permissions and platform restrictions. Use a narrow process or path filter to reduce output.

tools.name: strace
tools.summary: Trace system calls made by a process for local debugging and diagnostics.
tools.note: Android SELinux and ptrace restrictions may prevent tracing some processes. Trace only processes you own or are authorized to debug.
tools.trouble: If attach fails with Operation not permitted, check ptrace policy and SELinux restrictions. Installing strace does not grant extra process privileges.

tools.name: rsync
tools.summary: Synchronize files efficiently between local directories and trusted remote systems.
tools.note: Review source and destination carefully. Run with --dry-run before using --delete or other destructive options.
tools.trouble: For permission errors, inspect ownership and destination write access. For remote transfers, verify SSH connectivity and the remote rsync installation.

tools.name: bat
tools.summary: Syntax-highlighted file viewer with Git-aware line information.
tools.note: On Debian/Ubuntu the executable is commonly batcat; on Termux it is bat. Do not assume the command name is identical across distributions.
tools.trouble: If bat is not found on Debian/Ubuntu, try batcat. Check the package's installed executable name before adding an alias.

tools.name: Micro Editor
tools.summary: Modern terminal text editor with simple defaults and mouse support.
tools.note: Use a text editor only on files you intend to change. Keep backups of configuration files before editing them.
tools.trouble: If terminal colors or key bindings behave incorrectly, check TERM and terminal emulator compatibility. Start with a copy of important configuration files.

tools.name: aria2
tools.summary: Multi-protocol download utility with segmented transfer support.
tools.note: Use trusted URLs and verify checksums or signatures for downloaded software. Avoid downloading executable content from untrusted sources.
tools.trouble: For interrupted downloads, inspect the server response and local storage space. For certificate errors, repair the CA store rather than disabling TLS checks.

tools.name: UnZip
tools.summary: List and extract ZIP archives from the command line.
tools.note: List archive contents before extraction when files come from an untrusted source. Avoid extracting into privileged system directories.
tools.trouble: If extraction fails, check archive integrity and available storage. Use the list option to inspect filenames and paths before extracting.

tools.name: GNU Make
tools.summary: Run repeatable build and automation tasks described in Makefiles.
tools.note: A Makefile can run arbitrary shell commands. Inspect its targets and recipes before running make in an unfamiliar repository.
tools.trouble: For missing compiler or linker errors, install the documented build dependencies. Use make -n to preview recipes before executing them.

tools.name: CMake
tools.summary: Cross-platform build configuration and project generation tool.
tools.note: CMake configuration can invoke project scripts. Review CMakeLists.txt and presets before configuring an unfamiliar codebase.
tools.trouble: If compiler detection fails, install the compiler toolchain and make package. Clear or recreate the build directory after changing toolchain settings.

tools.name: Node.js
tools.summary: JavaScript runtime for CLI applications, tooling and local development.
tools.note: Use a project lockfile and review package scripts before running npm install or npm run. Dependency lifecycle scripts can execute code.
tools.trouble: If npm is missing, verify the distribution's Node.js package selection. If versions conflict, use a version manager from its official documentation.

tools.name: Ruby
tools.summary: Ruby runtime for scripts, automation and development tools.
tools.note: Prefer project-specific dependency management and review gem sources before installing packages.
tools.trouble: If gem installation fails, check RubyGems configuration and write permissions. Avoid running gem install with elevated privileges unless the official instructions require it.

tools.name: Perl
tools.summary: Perl interpreter for text processing, scripting and legacy automation.
tools.note: Review scripts before execution, especially when they process files or network input.
tools.trouble: If a module is missing, identify its package or distribution source first. Prefer system packages when available and avoid mixing incompatible library paths.

tools.name: PHP CLI
tools.summary: PHP command-line interpreter for scripts and local development tasks.
tools.note: The CLI package is for command-line use; it does not automatically configure a public web server. Keep test services bound to localhost unless intentionally exposed.
tools.trouble: If extensions are missing, install the matching extension package for the PHP version. Check php --ini to locate active configuration files.

tools.name: Go
tools.summary: Go compiler and toolchain for building portable command-line programs.
tools.note: Use module mode and review go.mod and go.sum before building unfamiliar projects.
tools.trouble: If a module cannot be downloaded, check GOPROXY and network access. Ensure the Go binary directory is on PATH when installing tools with go install.

tools.name: Rust Toolchain
tools.summary: Rust compiler for systems programming and native CLI tools.
tools.note: This entry installs the compiler package; Cargo availability can depend on the distribution package split. Check cargo --version before building Rust projects.
tools.trouble: If cargo is missing on Debian/Ubuntu, install the separate cargo package. For build errors, check the required Rust toolchain version in rust-toolchain.toml.

tools.name: Zsh
tools.summary: Interactive shell with advanced completion, globbing and customization.
tools.note: Changing the login shell affects startup behavior. Keep a working Bash session and back up shell configuration before switching.
tools.trouble: If startup becomes slow or broken, launch zsh with -f to skip user configuration and inspect .zshrc. Verify the shell path before changing the login shell.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.summary: Command-line multimedia inspection, conversion and stream processing.
tools.note: Conversion and transcoding can consume significant CPU, storage and battery. Preserve originals before overwriting media files.
tools.trouble: For unsupported codecs, inspect the build configuration with ffmpeg -buildconf. For permission errors, check input and output file access.

tools.name: GitHub CLI
tools.summary: Manage GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests and releases from the terminal.
tools.note: Authentication grants the CLI access to your GitHub account. Use least-privilege scopes and never expose tokens in logs or shell history.
tools.trouble: If authentication fails, run gh auth status and follow the official login flow. Check the active host and account before changing repository settings.

tools.name: Git LFS
tools.summary: Track large binary assets through Git Large File Storage.
tools.note: Git LFS transfers file contents to configured storage endpoints. Review repository attributes and storage policy before tracking large or sensitive files.
tools.trouble: If checkout shows pointer files, verify Git LFS is installed and run git lfs install for the current user. Check remote LFS quotas and authentication.

tools.name: BusyBox
tools.summary: Compact collection of common Unix command-line utilities in one binary.
tools.note: BusyBox applets can differ from GNU utilities in options and behavior. Do not assume scripts are fully portable between implementations.
tools.trouble: If an option is unsupported, check the BusyBox applet help and use the system's GNU utility where compatibility matters.

tools.name: GNU Coreutils
tools.summary: Essential file, text and system utilities such as ls, cp, mv, sort and wc.
tools.note: Coreutils commands can overwrite or delete files. Check source and destination paths before using cp, mv, rm or install.
tools.trouble: If an option differs, check the local command's --help because BusyBox and GNU implementations may not match. Confirm which binary is first on PATH.

tools.name: GNU Findutils
tools.summary: Find files and process directory trees with find, xargs and locate utilities.
tools.note: Review find expressions before adding -delete or piping results into commands that modify files.
tools.trouble: If results differ from expectations, quote patterns and test the expression without -delete or other actions first.

tools.name: GNU awk
tools.summary: Pattern scanning and data extraction for structured and line-oriented text.
tools.note: Awk programs process every matching input line. Test filters against sample data before applying them to production logs.
tools.trouble: If fields are misaligned, check the input delimiter and locale. Use a small sample to confirm field numbering before processing large files.

tools.name: less
tools.summary: Page through large text files and command output without loading everything into an editor.
tools.note: Use less -F or q to exit. When inspecting sensitive logs, remember terminal scrollback and copied output may retain data.
tools.trouble: If colors or control characters appear, try a plain-text view and check the program's color settings. Use / to search within the pager.

tools.name: Neovim
tools.summary: Extensible terminal text editor with Lua configuration and plugin support.
tools.note: Plugin managers and editor plugins execute code. Review plugin sources and back up configuration before adding extensions.
tools.trouble: If startup fails, run nvim --clean to bypass user configuration. Check the runtime path and plugin compatibility before reinstalling.

tools.name: GNU Debugger (GDB)
tools.summary: Inspect and debug native programs with breakpoints, stack traces and variable inspection.
tools.note: Debug only binaries and processes you own or are authorized to inspect. Android ptrace and SELinux policies may limit process attachment.
tools.trouble: If attach is denied, check ptrace permissions and platform policy. For missing symbols, rebuild with debug information and preserve the matching binary.

tools.name: proot-distro
tools.summary: Install and manage Linux root filesystems inside Termux using PRoot.
tools.note: This creates a user-space Linux environment, not a virtual machine or a separate Linux kernel. It does not automatically provide root privileges, monitor mode or direct hardware access.
tools.trouble: If a distribution fails to install, check free storage, Termux repository health and the selected distro support. Back up important files before removing a rootfs.

tools.name: Termux:API
tools.summary: Expose selected Android device functions to Termux command-line scripts through the companion app.
tools.note: The Termux:API Android companion app must be installed from the same signing source as the Termux app. Android permissions and API availability vary by device.
tools.trouble: If a command exists but returns no data, confirm the companion app is installed, signatures match and required Android permissions are granted.

tools.name: Termux Services
tools.summary: Service supervision helpers for managing supported background services in Termux.
tools.note: Service management can start processes in the background. Enable only services you understand and monitor their resource usage.
tools.trouble: If service commands are unavailable, restart the Termux session after installation and check the package's official usage guide.

roadmap.name: esptool
roadmap.purpose: Detect Espressif chips, inspect flash parameters, write firmware images and verify operations.
roadmap.safety: Flash erase and write operations can destroy existing firmware or data. The future guide will require chip identification, backup guidance and an explicit destructive-operation warning.

roadmap.name: ESP-IDF / idf.py
roadmap.purpose: Official Espressif development framework, build system, serial monitor and flashing workflow.
roadmap.safety: Versioned toolchain and board-specific setup will be documented before installation instructions are published.

roadmap.name: Arduino CLI
roadmap.purpose: Command-line board management, library installation, compilation and upload workflows.
roadmap.safety: Board identifiers, core versions and upload ports must be checked before any write operation.

roadmap.name: PlatformIO Core
roadmap.purpose: Embedded development environment for building, uploading and monitoring supported boards.
roadmap.safety: The guide will separate build, upload and monitor actions and will not assume every board uses the same serial port or boot mode.

roadmap.name: OpenOCD for ESP32
roadmap.purpose: Debug and program supported ESP32 targets through compatible JTAG adapters.
roadmap.safety: Requires compatible debug hardware and target configuration; it is not a universal USB flashing tool.

roadmap.name: Binwalk
roadmap.purpose: Inspect firmware images and identify embedded file systems and binary components.
roadmap.safety: Firmware extraction will be performed on copies in an isolated workspace; extracted content is untrusted.

roadmap.name: Tio Serial Terminal
roadmap.purpose: Serial console for boot logs, device interaction and embedded debugging.
roadmap.safety: Serial settings, port permissions and voltage levels must match the hardware. Never connect incompatible logic levels.

roadmap.name: USB-UART drivers (CP210x / CH34x)
roadmap.purpose: Identify and install the correct vendor driver for USB-to-serial adapters.
roadmap.safety: Drivers will be linked only from chip vendors. We will identify the adapter chipset before recommending a driver.
